summary: This defines a MarketProduct class: a single, unchangeable record of one item for sale at a farmers' market, holding its name, vendor, price, category, season, and whether it is organic. Later exercises in this chapter build lists of these objects and process them with streams.

lines.text: Marking a field `private final` means it is set once in the constructor and can never change afterwards, which makes the object safe to share across stream operations, including parallel ones.
Price is a `double` so it can hold values with cents, and later exercises will sum and average this field with `mapToDouble`.
A `boolean` field stores a plain yes-or-no fact, ideal for filtering the stream down to just the organic products.

lines.text: The constructor demands every value up front, so it is impossible to create a half-filled MarketProduct.
The parameter and the field share the name `name`, so `this.name` is needed to say "the field belonging to this object" rather than the parameter.
Because the fields are private, a getter is how outside code reads a value. Stream code will call these getters constantly inside lambdas.
Java convention names a getter for a boolean `isX` rather than `getX`, which is why this reads naturally as `product.isOrganic()`.
This annotation tells the compiler you intend to replace a method inherited from `Object`; if you misspell the method name, compilation fails instead of silently doing nothing.
Every object inherits a `toString`, but the default prints an unhelpful memory address. Overriding it means printing a product, or a whole list of them, shows readable field values.
The `'\''` is an escaped single quote character, so the output wraps text values in quotes and makes it obvious where a name starts and ends.
